title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 explains Lagrange's 1766-69 method (Misc. Taurinensia IV) for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y. Lagrange introduces an auxiliary 'time' t with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y. Differentiating gives second-order equations, and the variables p = x+y, q = x−y then yield first integrals; this is a mechanical analogy.

On this page, X = A+Bx+Cx², Y the same in y, and the equation is dx/√X + dy/√Y = 0, i.e. √Y is replaced by −√Y. From §33 (previous page) there are two forms of the complete algebraic integral:
(I) √X − √Y = √(Δ + 2B(x+y) + C(x+y)²), which comes from p'' = B + Cp;
(II) √X + √Y = √(Δ + C(x−y)²), which comes from q'' = Cq.

§34 treats the degenerate case where X and Y are perfect squares: X = (a+bx)², so A = a², B = 2ab, C = b². The equation becomes dx/(a+bx) + dy/(a+by) = 0.
- Form (I) gives b(x−y) = √(Δ + 4ab(x+y) + b²(x+y)²). Squaring gives −4b²xy = Δ + 4ab(x+y). After silently renaming the constant, this is Δ = a(x+y) + bxy.
- Euler verifies this by differentiating: a(dx+dy) + b(x dy + y dx) = 0, i.e. dx(a+by) + dy(a+bx) = 0, which is exactly the given equation.
- Form (II) gives 2a + b(x+y) = √(Δ + b²(x−y)²). Squaring and absorbing constants gives the same Γ = a(x+y) + bxy.
- Equivalently, (a+bx)(a+by) = const: the integral of the logarithmic equation, a multiplicative 'addition law'.

The page then opens the section 'Analysis' for the main case, where X and Y are general quartics A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ (the elliptic/Euler addition theorem). This is carried out on the following pages.
errors: Constants are renamed without comment. From −4b²xy = Δ + 4ab(x+y) one gets a(x+y) + bxy = −Δ/(4b), not Δ.
Similarly, in the second form the constant should be Γ = (Δ − 4a²)/(4b), not Δ − 4aa. Both slips are harmless because these are arbitrary constants.

ideas.what: Algebraic complete integral of dx/√X ± dy/√Y = 0 for quadratic X via Lagrange's auxiliary time variable and the substitutions p = x+y, q = x−y
ideas.modern_name: Addition formula for circular/logarithmic integrals derived by a mechanical (Lagrangian) method
ideas.where_published: E506 itself; cf. Euler's earlier E251/E252 and Institutiones calculi integralis I

ideas.what: Degenerate case of perfect-square radicands giving (a+bx)(a+by) = const
ideas.modern_name: Degeneration of the addition law to the multiplicative group law (logarithmic case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (implicit in his treatment of special cases)

ideas.what: Announcement of the analysis for quartic X and Y
ideas.modern_name: Euler addition theorem for elliptic integrals via Lagrange's method

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked special case and a section heading within Euler's exposition of Lagrange's known method. The mathematics is correct up to constant renaming, and nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The transcription of this page matches the image. The only notable point is that Δ is reused for a rescaled constant in the line 'Δ = a(x+y) + bxy', as printed.
On the previous page, 'X' − X'' should read 'X' − Y''.
